messages:
jamie: Heads-up, Rt cluster alert — rt-gpu-14 showing a steady climb in row remap / page retirement events. Grafana shows row_remap_count 3 -> 27 in ~48h. @oncall can you take a look?

oncall: on it. getting logs now. did we get any Xid / ECC errors alongside those?

sarah: I saw a few Xid 13s earlier today from that host. dmesg had repeated: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13". Could be memory corruption.

marta: node is rt-gpu-14 (rack5-slot3). GPU id 0 (PCI 65:00). gpustat shows GPU0: 24% mem err util 6% but that metric is noisy.

devin: quick checks: run these and paste outputs: 
```
ssh rt-gpu-14
sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 | grep -i xid
nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,RETIREMENT,DRIVER
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/0000:65:00.0/information
```

oncall: pasted snippets: dmesg: multiple "Xid 13" entries every ~10-30 mins. nvidia-smi shows ECC errors increasing and "Row remapping events: 27" under Retirement section.

jamie: thanks. Past experience: row remap count creeping up usually means aging DRAM rows; vendor recommendation is replace if remap > 20 and increasing. But we should confirm it's not software-induced: can we run memtest on that GPU and migrate workloads?

marta: I'll cordon and drain the node now: 
```
kubectl cordon node/rt-gpu-14
kubectl drain node/rt-gpu-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
```

sarah: also capture NVML logs and create nv-host diag bundle: 
```
sudo /usr/local/bin/nvidia-diag --collect --outfile /tmp/rt-gpu-14-diag.tgz
```

devin: recommend running vendor memtest (long) and quick stress (short) with pinned page allocation to provoke errors: prefer schedule during low traffic. If errors persist under no load that's hardware.

oncall: drain completed, pods rescheduled. I kicked off a quick memtest (30m) and the short run already repro'd ECC single-bit errors.

jamie: OK escalate: create ticket INF-4321 with logs, diag bundle, and row remap counts. Mark GPU for replacement if vendor confirms. Add automated watch to fleet-monitor: alert when row_remap_count >= 10 and delta > 5 in 24h.

marta: created ticket INF-4321 and attached diag bundle + dmesg. Noted host warranty: vendor SLA 72h replacement.

sarah: FYI, there was a similar pattern on ded-gpu-prod-03 last quarter — replacement solved it. We should also check neighboring hosts in same rack for correlated thermal issues.

devin: good point — thermal hist shows rt-rack5 mid-chiller sensor drifted higher by 3C in the last week. Could accelerate memory wear. I've filed infrainfra-thermal to inspect.

jamie: action items: 1) replacement approval + RMA (marta) 2) enable one-time eviction / tag GPU as "replace" in fleet inventory (oncall) 3) add alert rule for row remap deltas (devops) 4) run vendor memtest and confirm (devin)

oncall: tagged GPU in fleet inventory: state=drained,replacement_pending, ticket=INF-4321. Temporarily set allocation_policy to avoid scheduling on same PCI slot on other hosts.

marta: scheduling pickup with vendor. RMA pending. Will keep rt-gpu-14 off rotation until replacement verified.

jamie: also propose we add a nightly job to sample `/proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/retirement` and increment a timeseries for row_remap_count so we can trend over months. That will help predict replacements before hard failures.

devin: agree. I'll add a collector and a Grafana dashboard panel. Thresholds: warn at 5, critical at 15, auto-tickets when >20.

sarah: once replaced, run burn-in 24h and confirm row_remap stays 0 and no ECC. If replacement passes, reimage and return to pool.

jamie: thanks all. I'll update the incident channel and link INF-4321. Closing this thread for triage notes — keep updates in INF-4321. :thumbsup:

gpu-bot: automated note: alert resolved for rt-gpu-14 (node cordoned). Ticket INF-4321 created.
